To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Openness, interests, and cognitive abilities are important predictors of academic achievement in the psychology curriculum.

1) Openness and interest in Psychology predicted academic achievement, 2) Openness and interests predicted each other, 3) Openness, interest and academic achievement predicted working memory, 4) Openness and working memory predicted fluid intelligence, and 5) Openness, interests, working memory and fluid intelligence predicted each other.
Openness and interests are related to academic achievement and that this relation is mediated by fluid intelligence.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question how personality and cognitive abilities are related and how this relationship is related to academic success in higher education.
the interplay between personality and cognitive abilities in the prediction of academic achievement.
the role of cognitive ability and personality traits in the context of academic achievement.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Openness is a strong predictor for academic achievement, but the exact mechanisms are still not clear and need further research.
Openness and interest are relevant predictors of academic achievement and that fluid intelligence is not.
Openness, interests, working memory and fluid intelligence all have a significant influence on academic achievement, but their interplay is complex and not yet fully understood.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the OFCI model is not only valid for the prediction of crystallized intelligence, but also for academic achievements in general.
Openness, interests, cognitive abilities and academic achievement are not independent constructs.
Openness and interests are more important for achievement than fluid intelligence.
The main takeaway from our work is that
Openness, interest and cognitive ability are not only relevant predictors of academic achievement but also important factors for students' well-being and motivation.
the OFCI model can be applied to data from experience sampling studies.
Openness and interest in psychology are important predictors of academic achievement.
